title: Bringing Down Test Costs For Co-Packaged Optics
gist: In part three of a Semiconductor Engineering roundtable, test executives from Teradyne, Advantest, ISE Labs/ASE and Keysight say co-packaged optics test costs are approaching manufacturing cost, and that the economics shift toward pre-assembly screening because a cheap optical engine can scrap a $40,000-$50,000 GPU or ASIC. CPO is proven to work, so the problem is high-volume manufacturing, which needs standards and cooperation between photonics and semiconductor test teams.

insights.claim: An inexpensive optical engine cannot be allowed to take down a $40,000-$50,000 GPU or ASIC, which breaks the usual practice of setting test cost as a percentage of chip manufacturing cost and gives the companion optical chips an effectively unlimited test budget.
insights.speaker: Ira Leventhal
insights.so_what: Test intensity rises with scrap cost, benefiting test-equipment vendors in the CPO ramp.
insights.quote: You can’t have an inexpensive optical engine taking down a $40,000 or $50,000 GPU or ASIC
insights.locator: How does the economics of tests change

insights.claim: Rising device value, scrap cost, test complexity and package complexity make additional wafer-level or optical-engine-level testing more justifiable, shifting economics toward pre-assembly screening rather than traditional packaging test.
insights.speaker: Kazuo Yamaguchi
insights.so_what: Value in test moves upstream to wafer and engine-level insertions, away from final package test.
insights.quote: the economics are shifting toward pre-assembly screening rather than packaging test
insights.locator: How does the economics of tests change

insights.claim: Survey data from IPSR indicate the cost to test an optical component is approaching manufacturing cost and may exceed it as complexity rises, while GPU test cost on a percentage basis is peanuts by comparison.
insights.speaker: Dave Armstrong
insights.so_what: Industry must accept paying for known-good die, so money may shift across companies in the supply chain.
insights.quote: the cost to test an optical component is approaching the cost of manufacturing

insights.claim: End customers for AI accelerators and network switch devices are highly motivated to deploy as many as possible to generate more tokens, so testing these complex packages efficiently remains a continued focus.
insights.speaker: Matt Griffin
insights.so_what: Token-generation demand ties CPO test spend to hyperscaler AI capex.
insights.quote: highly motivated to deploy as many of these as possible into data centers so they can generate more tokens

insights.claim: Failure analysis starts with defining reference planes, the physical, electrical and optical boundaries at die pad, package balls, connectors or fiber interface, de-embedding everything between them and using the same boundaries across test insertions.
insights.speaker: Kazuo Yamaguchi
insights.so_what: Consistent boundary definitions are prerequisite for correlating test results across insertions.
insights.quote: We always look at the reference plane.
insights.locator: SE: How do you determine where failure originates

insights.claim: Customers are adding monitor photodiodes to light paths and loopback tap capability so unexpected transmit or receive results can be traced, though loopback-only testing can fail bit error rate without revealing why.
insights.speaker: Matt Griffin
insights.so_what: Diagnostic hooks in package design are becoming a design requirement.
insights.quote: customers add monitor photodiodes into their light paths
insights.locator: Griffin: We are seeing customers add monitor photodiodes

insights.claim: A golden reference laser source is a hot topic, but Advantest argues the laser is the functional equivalent of a device power supply, should be treated as a given, and the customer-preferred mission-mode laser is not an ATE instrument, so test equipment must evolve.
insights.speaker: Ira Leventhal
insights.so_what: Opens an instrument-category opportunity for ATE vendors if lasers become test-system components.
insights.quote: We call it a device power supply
insights.locator: Leventhal: I wanted to follow up about having a golden reference

insights.claim: Underperforming lasers are a substantial issue, which is why the golden reference is a hot topic in test.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Laser reliability is a key yield-risk for CPO modules.
insights.quote: Underperforming lasers are a substantial issue

insights.claim: Test for both NPO and CPO needs alignment of multiple optical connectors and power delivery, and while NPO's detachable engines could reduce the value of pre-attach coverage, customers still want known-good engines because rework and reattachment are painful.
insights.speaker: Matt Griffin
insights.so_what: Detachability does not remove the need for pre-attach screening.
insights.quote: reworking and reattaching further downstream is a real pain point
insights.locator: Griffin: When people say NPO and CPO

insights.claim: A retimed NPO has its own DSP and can be compliance-tested like a pluggable, but a linear-drive NPO removes the DSP so electrical and optical sides form one signal path, making test complexity the same as CPO.
insights.speaker: Kazuo Yamaguchi
insights.so_what: Linear-drive optics, favored for power, carry the hardest test and diagnosis burden.
insights.quote: A linear-drive NPO removes the DSP
insights.locator: Yamaguchi: A retimed NPO has its own DSP

insights.claim: CPO places far more on the package and needs ways of decoupling elements, with design for test helping engineers correlate individual-piece data to package failures.
insights.speaker: Ira Leventhal
insights.so_what: DFT investment is a prerequisite for CPO yield learning.
insights.quote: With CPO, you have a lot more stuff integrated onto the package
insights.locator: Leventhal: With CPO, you have a lot more stuff

insights.claim: High power dissipation is a further concern because CPO electrical signals cannot drive far, and the thermal behavior of the optical parts is a big deal.
insights.speaker: Dave Armstrong
insights.so_what: Thermal management links optics reliability to package design.
insights.quote: The thermal of all these optical parts is a big deal.
insights.locator: Armstrong: Another concern is high power dissipation

themes.theme: From proof of concept to high-volume manufacturing

insights.claim: The industry no longer has to prove CPO works, since Meta presented strong reliability data this year; the challenge is high-volume manufacturing, an ecosystem problem handled near-term with extra screen-in, burn-in and insertions.
insights.speaker: Ira Leventhal
insights.so_what: Near-term CPO ramp will add test insertions, supporting equipment demand before efficiency gains arrive.
insights.quote: it’s no longer a challenge to prove that CPO works

insights.claim: NPO has a lower hurdle to get running and its learnings should bootstrap CPO toward HVM, though that will not be a slam dunk.
insights.speaker: Ira Leventhal
insights.so_what: NPO is likely to ramp ahead of CPO and to supply manufacturing learning.
insights.quote: It’s a lower hurdle to jump over

insights.claim: Industry is moving so fast that standards bodies cannot keep up, yet standards and MSAs are needed to manufacture at scale with multiple parts sources and to align test platforms, without changing the measurement science.
insights.speaker: Ira Leventhal
insights.so_what: Standards lag is a supply-chain bottleneck for multi-sourcing CPO parts.
insights.quote: The industry is moving so fast that standards bodies can’t keep up.

insights.claim: Customers have separate photonics groups, used to small-scale device testing, and semiconductor high-volume test groups that prioritize uptime, serviceability and modularity, and these trade-offs can lower optical performance, so internal alignment is needed.
insights.speaker: Matt Griffin
insights.so_what: Organizational friction inside customers, not only technology, will gate CPO ramp timing.
insights.quote: two different groups within that company

insights.claim: Training in electro-optics is critical to understanding design and test tradeoffs, and a wider community of partners is needed to build a scalable high-volume production structure.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Workforce skills overlap between photonics and semiconductor test is scarce.
